passage: Thirty days to the exam, and Shreya's syllabus list ran to two pages. She sat on her bed in Bengaluru with three coloured pens. Beside each topic she wrote two numbers: how many marks it usually carries, and how sure she felt, from one to five. Topics with high marks and confidence five could wait; they were already safe. Topics with tiny marks and confidence one could wait too, or be dropped. The middle was where her hours would pay most: high marks, confidence three. Her friend Disha peeked over her shoulder. "That looks like a hospital chart." "It is a triage," Shreya said. "Fix first whatever improves most per hour."

"Thirty days," Farhan said, dropping onto the library bench. "And sixty topics. I'm going to die."
"You're not going to revise sixty topics," Trisha said. "Rate them."
"Rate them how?"
"Two numbers. How many marks it carries, and how sure you are, one to three."
Farhan scribbled. "Organic: big marks, confidence one. Periodic table: small marks, three. Electrochemistry: big marks, two."
"Which gives you the most per hour?"
He thought. "Not organic, that would take weeks. Not periodic, I already know it... Electrochemistry. Big marks, and I half know it."
"So?"
"So the twos with big marks go first. Then organic. The threes last, just a quick look."
Trisha grinned. "Look at you, planning."
"Don't. I'm still going to die. Just more efficiently."

qa.q: Why do big-mark, medium-confidence topics give the most per hour?
qa.a: They carry many marks and are already half known, so a few hours turn them into secure marks, unlike weak topics that need weeks or strong ones that gain little.

passage: I'm Nirmala, and with thirty days left before the Biology board exam I made the most useful table of my life. My brother Kunal had watched me reread chapter one for the third time. "You're doing the easy one again," he said. He was right. So I listed all sixteen chapters and gave each two scores: the marks it usually carries, and my confidence, low, medium or high. Genetics: lots of marks, medium. Plant physiology: lots of marks, low. Diversity of life: few marks, high. Then I asked myself where one hour buys the most. Not the high-confidence ones; I'd gain nothing. Not the lowest yet; they'd swallow a week. The medium ones with big marks. Genetics went first. By the exam, genetics felt solid, and I had still reached plant physiology.
